title: New Zealand has a new official language — English
facts: The New Zealand Parliament passed the English Language Bill establishing English as an official language.
The English Language Bill establishes English alongside Māori and New Zealand Sign Language as official languages.
Government data from 2023 showed over 95% of New Zealand's population spoke English.
Government statistics indicate 4.3% of New Zealand's population spoke Māori in 2023.
New Zealand Sign Language was used by 0.5% of the country's population in 2023.
The nationalist New Zealand First party championed the English Language Bill in parliament.
Green Party Member of Parliament Tamatha Paul spoke against the English Language Bill during parliamentary debate.
Te reo Māori was the primary spoken language in New Zealand prior to British colonization in 1840.
Te reo Māori was formally designated an official language of New Zealand in the 1980s.
The 1730 Proceedings in Courts of Justice Act mandated the use of English in English courtrooms.
Labour MP Camilla Belich participated in parliamentary debates concerning the language bill.
The New Zealand Parliament's Justice Committee received 1,601 written public submissions regarding the bill.
Nearly two-thirds of public submissions submitted to the Justice Committee opposed the English Language Bill.
New Zealand First MP Casey Costello defended the language legislation during its third reading.
The English Language Bill does not introduce new legal requirements for government document administration.
